field_definitions.name: method or result
field_definitions.year: publication year of the version cited
field_definitions.exact_claim: the claim as the source states it, numbers included
field_definitions.regime_of_validity: the assumptions outside which the claim does not hold
field_definitions.applies_here: YES / PARTIAL / NO / PRIOR-ART, with reason
field_definitions.implication: what it means for this sprint's architecture
field_definitions.verified: primary = abstract or full text fetched this session; secondary = search-result snippet only, treat numbers as provisional

_meta.caveat: Rows marked verified=secondary have NOT had their primary source read in full. Do not put a secondary number in a headline without opening the paper.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: TALOS-N
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: "Validation on an independent set of proteins indicates that backbone torsion angles can be predicted for a larger, >=90% fraction of the residues, with an error rate smaller than ca 3.5%, and a root mean square difference between predicted and crystallographically observed (phi,psi) torsion angles of ca 12 deg." Side-chain chi1 rotamer information for about half of those residues.
strand_1_torsion_channel.evaluation_setting: Independent set of FOLDED GLOBULAR PROTEINS with complete or near-complete backbone shift assignments, scored against CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC (phi,psi). Matching is against a database of 9523 proteins. The 12 deg figure is computed over the residues that were predicted, i.e. AFTER the >=10% declined and the 3.5% erroneous are removed.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: (a) Predictability gate: the centre residue is predictable only if at least two of residues {i-1,i,i+1} have at least three assigned chemical shifts. (b) Matching unit is a HEPTAPEPTIDE (+/-3 residues); classification is 'Strong' when all 25 best-matching heptapeptides agree, 'Generous' when only the top 10 do. (c) Residues with RCI-S2 <= 0.6 are classified 'Dyn' and carry no usable torsion restraint. (d) Reference is a rigid crystal structure, so the 12 deg is a rigid-body accuracy, not an accuracy against a solution ensemble.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: PARTIAL - the number is real but every gate above bites hardest on an isolated 9-16-mer. On a 13-mer, 6 of 13 residues have a truncated +/-3 window; an isolated peptide in water is by construction low-S2, so a large fraction would classify 'Dyn'. Both failure modes are CLUSTERED (termini, flexible segments), not random.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: Do NOT assume 90% coverage on this target class. Measure realised coverage on the 79 BMRB-linked targets from shifts alone before building anything. Sprint 12's curve makes the channel worth ~+0.08 A (i.e. nothing) at 50% coverage.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: TALOS-N protocol chapter
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: Worked example (DinI, 81 residues): 71 unambiguous predictions (70 'Strong', 1 'Generous'), 2 ambiguous, 6 dynamic. Residue M1 shows no prediction. 'Dyn' assigned when RCI-S2 <= 0.6. Predictability rule: >=3 chemical shifts on >=2 of {i-1,i,i+1}.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: One example, not a benchmark. 71/81 = 87.7% on a FOLDED protein with a near-complete shift set; the residual is 6 dynamic + 2 ambiguous + terminal.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: YES as a mechanism reference - it is the clearest published statement of the exact gates that decide coverage.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: The mechanism, not the headline, is what transfers. Cite this for the gap-clustering argument: the declined residues in the worked example are the dynamic ones and the N-terminus, i.e. contiguous, which is exactly the case Sprint 12's fill_pool experiment shows is worst.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: TALOS+
strand_1_torsion_channel.venue: J Biomol NMR 44:213-223 (Shen, Delaglio, Cornilescu, Bax)
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: Unambiguous ('Good') prediction rate 88.5%, error rate 2.46%; excluding the ~2.5% of residues where prediction strongly differs from the crystal state, accuracy of predicted phi and psi is +/-13 deg. Extending the database from 20 to 200 proteins raised coverage 65% -> 74% and cut the error rate 3% -> 2.5%.
strand_1_torsion_channel.evaluation_setting: Folded proteins; database of X-ray structures better than 2.0 A resolution and chain length > 20 residues.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: Same heptapeptide-window and shift-completeness gates as TALOS-N. The reference database EXCLUDES chains of <= 20 residues, so nothing in its training or validation resembles a 9-16-mer.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: PARTIAL - superseded by TALOS-N, but the database-construction detail (>20 residues) is the direct evidence that short peptides are out of distribution.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: Strong, citable statement that the TALOS family's reference corpus contains no peptides of this project's length. Any transfer claim is extrapolation.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: SPARTA+
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: Neural network trained on 580 proteins with high-resolution X-ray structures and near-complete backbone + 13Cbeta shifts. RMS prediction errors 2.45, 1.09, 0.94, 1.14, 0.25, 0.49 ppm for 15N, 13C', 13Calpha, 13Cbeta, 1Halpha, 1HN.
strand_1_torsion_channel.evaluation_setting: Structure -> chemical shift, on folded proteins with X-ray references.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: This is the FORWARD map. SPARTA+ takes coordinates and returns shifts. It does not and cannot return torsion angles from shifts.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: NO as a torsion channel - the brief lists it alongside TALOS as a torsion predictor, which is a category error. YES as an OBJECTIVE-VALIDITY instrument.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: CORRECTION: remove SPARTA+ from the torsion-prior list. Repurpose it: for a candidate structure, predict shifts and score agreement against the deposited BMRB shifts. That is a native-coordinate-free reranking signal and a direct test of brief section 5 (does the objective rank the native?).

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: SHIFTX2
strand_1_torsion_channel.venue: J Biomol NMR 50:43-57 (Han, Liu, Ginzinger, Wishart)
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: Significantly improved structure-based chemical shift prediction over SPARTA+ by combining an empirical/ML module with a sequence-homology-based transfer module.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: Forward map only. Its homology-transfer module looks up structurally homologous proteins with assigned shifts - a direct memorisation path.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: PARTIAL - usable as a forward validity instrument but the transfer module is a leakage risk; use the ML module only.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: If SPARTA+/SHIFTX2 are used as a reranker, disable homology transfer and label the arm.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: Random Coil Index / RCI-S2
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: RCI-S2 scales 0 (total disorder) to 1 (fully rigid). Standard practice excludes residues with RCI-derived S2 <= 0.7 from torsion-angle restraint generation because those coil regions are too flexible to yield reliable torsion angles; TALOS-N uses a <= 0.6 threshold for its 'Dyn' label.
strand_1_torsion_channel.evaluation_setting: NMR protein structures with disordered or poorly defined regions.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: S2 derived from secondary shifts; it reports on ps-ns backbone order.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: YES - this is the single mechanism that most threatens coverage on isolated 9-16-mers.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: The coverage number this project needs is not 'what does TALOS-N quote' but 'what fraction of residues in an isolated peptide have RCI-S2 > 0.6'. Compute it directly from the deposited shifts of the 79 BMRB-linked targets - RCI needs only shifts and sequence. This is the cheapest kill-or-continue experiment in the sprint.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: SPOT-1D-LM
strand_1_torsion_channel.venue: Scientific Reports 12:7607 (Singh, Paliwal, Litfin, Singh, Zhou)
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: phi/psi MAE in degrees: TEST2018 SPOT-1D-LM 15.99 / 23.74; SPOT-1D (profile) 16.88 / 24.87; SPOT-1D-Single 22.16 / 40.58. TEST2020 SPOT-1D-LM 20.67 / 36.57; SPOT-1D 20.33 / 34.46; SPOT-1D-Single 22.92 / 44.25.
strand_1_torsion_channel.evaluation_setting: TEST2018 = 250 proteins released Jan-Jun 2018, resolution < 2.5 A, R-free < 0.25, < 25% identity to pre-2018 proteins. TEST2020 = 671 proteins, homologs removed by HMM, length <= 1024. Neff1-2020 = 46 proteins with no homologs.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: Full-length crystallised domains. No short-peptide test set; nothing at 9-16 residues. Single-sequence performance (Neff1) is the closest analogue to a peptide with no MSA and is materially worse.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: YES - this is the honest ceiling of the DEPLOYABLE, sequence-only torsion channel.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: DECISIVE. Best sequence-only psi MAE is 23.7-36.6 deg on full proteins. Sprint 12's own curve gives 2.408 A at sigma=20 deg with FULL coverage. A sequence-only torsion prior therefore lands ~2.4-2.9 A - better than the 3.213 A incumbent, but it does not reach 2.0 A. Stop treating sequence-only torsion prediction as the route to the target.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: SPOT-1D-Single
strand_1_torsion_channel.evaluation_setting: As above, single-sequence input, no MSA, no language model.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: YES - the true no-MSA floor, and a 13-mer has an MSA of depth ~1.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: If a torsion predictor is retrained locally under leave-fold-out, this is the realistic prior for what it will deliver: psi error 40+ deg. Sprint 12's own LFO 4-state torsion-bin predictor (0.690 overall, 0.517 on FAIL18) is consistent with this and should be reported alongside it rather than as an isolated disappointment.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: DCMA (dilated convolution + multi-head attention torsion predictor)
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: Lightweight sequence-based predictor of backbone (phi,psi); presented as faster than prior deep models at comparable accuracy.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: PARTIAL - a 2024 successor, but no evidence of a regime change in accuracy.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: No 2024-2026 sequence-only method was found that materially beats the SPOT-1D-LM MAE band. Treat ~16 deg phi / ~24 deg psi as the state of the art and do not budget for improvement from this direction.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: OPUS-TASS2
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: Ensemble CNN/LSTM/transformer predictor of backbone dihedrals and secondary structure; SOTA on standard sets prior to 2024.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: Same as DCMA: the sequence-only band is stable.

strand_1_torsion_channel.name: APPTEST (short-peptide structure prediction)
strand_1_torsion_channel.venue: Briefings in Bioinformatics (carried over from s12/lit_FINDINGS.md)
strand_1_torsion_channel.exact_claim: 1.96 A mean RMSD on 42 short peptides with deployable selection, using a distance + torsion prediction head.
strand_1_torsion_channel.regime_of_validity: Its own peptide set, not this project's 126-target instrument.
strand_1_torsion_channel.applies_here: YES as the classical number to beat.
strand_1_torsion_channel.implication: Sub-2.0 A is attainable at this length by SOME architecture, and the one that does it uses a torsion head. That supports the torsion direction and simultaneously sets the bar: a quantum architecture that lands at 2.4 A is not competitive on accuracy and must be sold on the trainability study instead.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Barren plateaus in quantum neural network training landscapes
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: Nature Communications 9:4812 (McClean, Boixo, Smelyanskiy, Babbush, Neven)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: For a randomly initialised parameterised circuit that forms a 2-design, the expectation of the gradient of the cost is zero and its variance vanishes exponentially in the number of qubits.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: REQUIRES (a) random initialisation, (b) the circuit ensemble approximating a unitary 2-design, i.e. sufficient depth/expressibility. It says nothing about a structured, shallow, or warm-started ansatz, and nothing about a specific fixed parameter point.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: PARTIAL - applies only if the ansatz used is deep/expressive enough to 2-design. An MPS or shallow chain ansatz with bond dimension capped at 2^layers is explicitly NOT in this regime.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: Do not cite McClean 2018 to explain any flatness observed with the repo's MPSAnsatz or a shallow StatevectorCircuit. Misapplying the 2-design assumption is the single most common way this audience dismisses a trainability claim.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Cost function dependent barren plateaus in shallow parametrized quantum circuits
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: Nature Communications 12:1791 (Cerezo, Sone, Volkoff, Cincio, Coles)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: "We rigorously prove two results, assuming V(theta) is an alternating layered ansatz composed of blocks forming local 2-designs." (1) Cost defined by GLOBAL observables gives exponentially vanishing gradients even when V is SHALLOW. (2) Cost defined by LOCAL observables gives at worst a polynomially vanishing gradient so long as the depth of V is O(log n).
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: Alternating layered ansatz, blocks forming LOCAL 2-designs. The local-cost guarantee holds only up to O(log n) depth; between O(log n) and poly(n) the variance interpolates from polynomial to exponential decay. It is a statement about observable locality in the PAULI basis of the qubits being varied.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES, and it is the single most directly relevant theorem in the sprint. Both Legacy and AMBER are DIAGONAL in the torsion bitstring basis, hence each is exactly a weighted sum of Pauli-Z strings. Their Pauli-weight distributions are the 'globality' this theorem is about.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: This turns brief section 4 from an intuition into a measurement. Compute the Walsh-Hadamard (Pauli-Z) spectrum of E(bitstring) for both energy models - exactly for n_bits <= ~20, by sampling above - and report the weight distribution. The prediction is that AMBER's spectral mass sits at higher Pauli weight than Legacy's, and the theorem then predicts worse gradient scaling. That is the sprint's headline mechanism, it is cheap, and it is classical.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Noise-induced barren plateaus (NIBP)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: Nature Communications 12:6961 (Wang, Fontana, Cerezo, Sharma, Sone, Cincio, Coles)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: For local Pauli noise, the gradient vanishes exponentially in the number of qubits n if the ansatz depth grows linearly with n. Under unital noise the loss concentrates deterministically toward Tr[O]/2^n as depth L increases.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: REQUIRES a noisy device and depth growing with n. NIBP is DETERMINISTIC concentration - it is not cured by clever initialisation, and error mitigation does not remove it. It is conceptually distinct from the random-initialisation BP.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: NO for this sprint's numbers - the repo runs exact statevector, exact MPS and lightning.qubit, i.e. noiseless simulation. It applies to any hardware claim.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: Explicitly state that no NIBP result is being claimed and that all measurements are noiseless. If a reviewer asks about hardware relevance, the honest answer is that this sprint measures the noiseless landscape only, and NIBP would be an additional, independent obstruction.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Entanglement-induced barren plateaus
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: Excess entanglement between visible and hidden/traced-out subsystems hinders learning; circuits satisfying a volume law encounter exponentially flat landscapes. In the Lie-algebraic restatement, a DETERMINISTIC BP occurs when the initial state's projection onto the relevant module is O(1/2^n).
strand_2_barren_plateaus.evaluation_setting: Quantum neural networks with hidden units; analytic + numerics.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: REQUIRES volume-law entanglement between the measured and unmeasured parts, or an initial state with exponentially small module projection. A product-state initialisation with a shallow chain ansatz is not in this regime.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: PARTIAL - relevant only if the sprint warm-starts from, or evolves into, a volume-law state. The chain-topology bond-dimension cap of 2^layers is an explicit entanglement bound, which is a defensible reason this mechanism is not active.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: The bond-dimension cap is an asset, not a limitation: it is a quantitative bound on the entanglement, and therefore a defensible argument that observed flatness is NOT entanglement-induced. Report the entanglement entropy across the chain cut alongside the gradient variance to close this alternative explanation.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Connecting ansatz expressibility to gradient magnitudes and barren plateaus
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: Gradient magnitude is bounded by circuit expressibility: the more expressive the ansatz, the more the loss concentrates and the smaller the gradients.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.evaluation_setting: General parameterised circuits; bounds relating expressibility measures to gradient variance.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: A bound, not an equality - low expressibility does not guarantee trainability.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES - it is the correct framing for an ansatz-side control in this sprint.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: If Legacy and AMBER are run on the SAME ansatz (as the brief mandates), expressibility is held fixed by construction and cannot explain any difference between them. Say so explicitly - it is what makes the comparison controlled.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Lie-algebraic theory of barren plateaus
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: Nature Communications 15:7172 (Ragone, Bakalov, Sauvage, Kemper, Ortiz Marrero, Larocca, Cerezo)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: For circuits forming a 2-design over their dynamical Lie algebra, Var[loss] = P_M(rho) P_M(O) / dim(M): exponentially large dim(M), or exponentially small projection of the initial state or the observable onto the accessible module, each gives a barren plateau.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: REQUIRES the circuit to 2-design over its DLA. Provides a single formula unifying expressibility, observable-globality and entanglement mechanisms.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES conceptually - it is the cleanest way to explain why the OBSERVABLE (the energy model) can move the variance with everything else fixed. P_M(O) is exactly the observable-dependent factor.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: This is the theoretical hook for the whole sprint: with rho, U(theta) and dim(M) held fixed across arms, ANY variance difference between Legacy and AMBER is attributable to P_M(O). State the hypothesis in that language and the audience will recognise it immediately.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Barren plateaus in variational quantum computing (review)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: Nature Reviews Physics (Larocca, Thanasilp, Wang, Sharma, Biamonte, Coles, Cincio, McClean, Holmes, Cerezo)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: "all the moving pieces of an algorithm -- choices of ansatz, initial state, observable, loss function and hardware noise -- can lead to BPs when ill-suited". Distinguishes PROBABILISTIC BPs (with narrow gorges: minima whose relative volume in parameter space is exponentially small) from DETERMINISTIC concentration (noise, over-entangled states), and separates BPs from the distinct problem of exponentially many poor local minima.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: Each mechanism carries its own assumptions; the review is explicit that a log-depth hardware-efficient ansatz can still show a BP for a non-local measurement.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES - the canonical citation and the correct taxonomy.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: Use the review's taxonomy verbatim in the findings so that each claim is attached to its mechanism. In particular: 'log-depth + local cost avoids BPs' is FALSE as stated; it requires the observable to lie in a polynomially large module.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Does provable absence of barren plateaus imply classical simulability?
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: Nature Communications 16 (Cerezo, Larocca, Garcia-Martin, Diaz, Braccia, Fontana, Rudolph, Bermejo, Ijaz, Thanasilp, Anschuetz, Holmes)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: Case-by-case evidence that many commonly used models whose landscapes provably avoid barren plateaus also admit classical simulation, provided one can collect classical data from the quantum device in an initial data-acquisition phase. Described by the authors as "a soft form of dequantization". Mechanism: BP-avoidance works by confining the evolved observable to a polynomially large subspace, and the loss then becomes an inner product in that reduced space.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.evaluation_setting: Survey of model families with provable BP absence.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: Evidence, not a theorem; the argument requires a classical data-acquisition phase and does not cover every BP-free family. It attacks the INFORMATION-PROCESSING advantage, not the ability to run the circuit.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES, and it is the most dangerous unaddressed critique of the sprint's quantum framing.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: The repository already runs exact statevector and exact MPS simulation of its own circuits - i.e. it is a live instance of this critique. Address it head-on: state that every number is classically simulated, that no quantum advantage is claimed, and that the contribution is a controlled measurement of how problem structure shapes VQA landscapes. Do not let this be the reviewer's discovery.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Quantum variational algorithms are swamped with traps
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: A wide class of variational quantum models that are SHALLOW and exhibit NO barren plateaus nonetheless have only a superpolynomially small fraction of local minima within any constant energy of the global minimum, rendering them untrainable absent a good initial guess.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: Requires random initialisation and the specific model class analysed. Does not apply to warm-started or structurally-initialised optimisation.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: Absence of a barren plateau is NOT evidence of trainability. If the sprint reports 'AMBER shows no worse gradient variance than Legacy', that is not a conclusion that AMBER is trainable. Report solution QUALITY (native percentile, Spearman rho vs CA-RMSD, distance of argmin to native) as a separate axis from gradient variance, exactly as brief section 5 demands.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: CVaR-VQE (Improving variational quantum optimization using CVaR)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: Replacing the expectation value with the CVaR of the measured energy distribution (average over the best alpha-fraction of samples) improves the performance of variational optimisation for combinatorial problems.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.evaluation_setting: Combinatorial optimisation with DIAGONAL cost Hamiltonians.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: Applies where the cost is diagonal and one wants a good BITSTRING, not a good expectation value. CVaR is not the expectation of an observable, so theorems stated for <H> do not transfer mechanically.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES - this is exactly the sprint's setting (energy is a function of the torsion bitstring).
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: Correct precedent to cite. But note the framing consequence: because the cost is diagonal, the algorithm is a variational quantum SAMPLER over a classical objective, not an eigensolver for a quantum Hamiltonian. Say that plainly; this audience will notice, and pre-empting it is worth more than the word 'VQE'.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Quantum Tilted Loss in Variational Optimization
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: Tilting "does not remove the barren plateau problem by itself": fixed tilts show exponential-in-n decay of gradient variance identical to standard objectives. Aggressive tilting shifts the bottleneck "from trainability to estimability: from a flat landscape to a larger sampling overhead". As alpha decreases in CVaR, the effective sample size shrinks proportionally, demanding a strict increase in total measurement budget. QTL is a smooth lower-tail counterpart of CVaR with CVaR_alpha(theta) >= L_gamma(theta) + (1/gamma) log(1/alpha). Dynamic tilt schedules scaling as Theta(-n) can achieve polynomial lower bounds in structured settings.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: Fixed-tilt result is general; the polynomial-lower-bound result requires structured settings and an n-dependent schedule.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES - directly governs the sprint's CVaR usage.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: TWO CORRECTIONS. (1) Never present CVaR as a barren-plateau mitigation; it is not. (2) Budget parity in objective evaluations is NOT budget parity in SHOTS once alpha differs between arms. If Legacy and AMBER are run at the same alpha this is neutral, but any alpha sweep must report shots-to-fixed-gradient-SNR, or brief rule 9 is silently violated.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Hamiltonian variational ansatz without barren plateaus
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: Quantum 8:1239 (Park, Killoran et al. / Larocca line)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: Hamiltonian-variational ansaetze generated by a local Hamiltonian are shown not to have exponentially small gradients under stated conditions.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: Requires the ansatz generators to be the problem Hamiltonian's local terms and a restricted DLA.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: NO for the current design, but it is the ONE exception that matters for strand 3 - see the geometry note.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: If the sprint ever adopts a Hamiltonian-generated ansatz, the state manifold itself becomes energy-model-dependent and the Fubini-Study metric legitimately differs between Legacy and AMBER. With a problem-independent ansatz it cannot. Choose deliberately and say which.

strand_2_barren_plateaus.name: Peptide conformational sampling using QAOA
strand_2_barren_plateaus.venue: npj Quantum Information 9:70 (Boulebnane, Lucas, Meyder, Adaszewski, Montanaro)
strand_2_barren_plateaus.exact_claim: "based on numerical simulations on 20 qubits, we find less promising results: deep quantum circuits are required to achieve accurate results, and the performance of QAOA can be matched by random sampling up to a small overhead. Overall, these results cast serious doubt on the ability of QAOA to address the protein folding problem in the near term, even in an extremely simplified setting."
strand_2_barren_plateaus.evaluation_setting: 20-qubit noiseless simulation; self-avoiding walks first, then folding with a simplified physical potential.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.regime_of_validity: QAOA specifically, simplified potential, 20 qubits, near-term depths. Does not rule out other variational forms, but the burden of proof has shifted.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.applies_here: YES - the most important negative control in the whole literature for this sprint.
strand_2_barren_plateaus.implication: MANDATORY CONTROL: a random-sampling arm at MATCHED objective-evaluation budget, for both energy models. Without it, any 'the VQE found a good structure' result is presumed refuted by this paper. Sprint 12's own record (a certified exact optimum emitted 0.169 A worse than its anchor) points the same way.

strand_3_information_geometry.name: Quantum Natural Gradient
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: "The optimization dynamics is interpreted as moving in the steepest descent direction with respect to the Quantum Information Geometry, corresponding to the real part of the Quantum Geometric Tensor (QGT), also known as the Fubini-Study metric tensor. An efficient algorithm is presented for computing a block-diagonal approximation to the Fubini-Study metric tensor for parametrized quantum circuits."
strand_3_information_geometry.regime_of_validity: PURE states, unitary circuits, exact (or well-estimated) metric. The metric g_ij(theta) = Re[<d_i psi|d_j psi> - <d_i psi|psi><psi|d_j psi>] is a function of the state family |psi(theta)> = U(theta)|psi_0> ONLY. It contains no reference to the observable being minimised.
strand_3_information_geometry.applies_here: YES, and it settles the question the brief flags.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: THE KEY CORRECTION FOR THE GEOMETRY AGENT. With a problem-independent ansatz and a fixed input state, Legacy and AMBER CANNOT produce different metrics at the same theta. They produce different GRADIENTS, hence different trajectories theta(t), hence different metric values VISITED. Every geometry sentence must be phrased as 'the energy model selects a region of a fixed state manifold'. Use metric equality at matched random theta across arms as a unit test on the code - if it differs, there is a bug or an unintended Hamiltonian-dependent ansatz.
strand_3_information_geometry.verified: primary (abstract); metric-independence is the standard definition

strand_3_information_geometry.name: Block-diagonal and diagonal approximations to the QGT
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: The block-diagonal approximation computes the metric only within each layer of parameters, requiring one extra circuit per layer; the diagonal approximation keeps only g_ii and reduces QNG to a per-parameter rescaled gradient.
strand_3_information_geometry.regime_of_validity: The approximation discards inter-layer correlations. It is exact only when the metric is block-diagonal, which the layered structure does not guarantee.
strand_3_information_geometry.applies_here: YES if QNG is used at all.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: If the sprint reports a QNG arm, report WHICH approximation. A diagonal-QNG result is a preconditioned SGD result and must not be described as natural-gradient descent on the state manifold.

strand_3_information_geometry.name: Metric singularity and regularisation in QNG
strand_3_information_geometry.venue: multiple (PennyLane docs; Phys Scr 2025 geodesic corrections; Springer 2025 trust-region)
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: The Fubini-Study metric is generically SINGULAR under redundant parameterisation, so QNG updates are ill-posed; standard practice uses the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse or Tikhonov regularisation g + lambda*I. Reported curvature can depend on the regularisation: for Tikhonov, the curvature at a point can be ill-defined because its value depends on how lambda is taken to zero. Optimisation trajectories can pass through genuinely singular points (e.g. frustration-free Hamiltonians where the optimum is singular).
strand_3_information_geometry.regime_of_validity: Non-singularity holds in most of parameter space but the condition number is not controlled.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: Any curvature/eigenvalue-spectrum result must state lambda and show it is stable under a lambda sweep. Reporting a metric eigenvalue spectrum without the regulariser is a result that can be argued away. Report the CONDITION NUMBER and the RANK of the metric (effective quantum dimension) rather than raw eigenvalues, since those are the regularisation-robust quantities.

strand_3_information_geometry.name: Capacity and quantum geometry of parametrized quantum circuits
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: The rank of the quantum Fisher information / QGT gives the EFFECTIVE QUANTUM DIMENSION: the number of independent directions the circuit can actually move the state in. Redundant parameters show up as a rank deficit, and circuits saturating their dimension are over-parameterised.
strand_3_information_geometry.evaluation_setting: Parameterised circuits of varying depth and topology.
strand_3_information_geometry.regime_of_validity: Ansatz property only; observable-independent. Rank measured numerically at finite precision - depends on the eigenvalue cutoff chosen.
strand_3_information_geometry.applies_here: YES - this is the correct ansatz-side diagnostic, and it is HAMILTONIAN-INDEPENDENT by construction.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: Report effective quantum dimension once per ansatz, NOT once per energy model. It is a property of the shared apparatus. Doing so demonstrates the comparison is controlled, and pre-empts the reviewer's first question about whether the two arms had the same expressive power.

strand_3_information_geometry.name: The power of quantum neural networks (effective dimension)
strand_3_information_geometry.venue: Nature Computational Science 1:403 (Abbas, Sutter, Zoufal, Lucchi, Figalli, Woerner)
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: Uses the Fisher information spectrum to define an effective dimension and links a flat/degenerate Fisher spectrum to slow training; well-conditioned Fisher spectra correlate with faster convergence.
strand_3_information_geometry.regime_of_validity: CLASSICAL Fisher information of the model output distribution, NOT the quantum Fisher information of the state - the two are different objects and are routinely conflated.
strand_3_information_geometry.applies_here: PARTIAL, and mainly as a warning.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: Be explicit about WHICH Fisher information is being reported. For a CVaR objective over sampled bitstrings the natural object is the CLASSICAL Fisher information of the measurement distribution p_theta(x) - and unlike the QGT, that one DOES depend on the measurement basis but still not on the energy model. Getting this distinction wrong in a talk to this professor would be costly.

strand_3_information_geometry.name: Quantum natural gradient generalised to noisy and non-unitary circuits
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: Extends QNG to mixed states; for mixed states the relevant metric is a quantum Fisher information that is no longer the pure-state Fubini-Study metric.
strand_3_information_geometry.applies_here: NO for the noiseless simulations this sprint runs.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: Confirms the pure-state Fubini-Study metric is the correct object here, and gives the citation for why noisy hardware would require a different one.

strand_3_information_geometry.name: Efficient Hamiltonian-aware Quantum Natural Gradient Descent for VQE
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: "Hamiltonian-aware" means selectively COMPUTING metric blocks that matter for a given Hamiltonian structure, reducing metric evaluations. The geometric tensor itself is unchanged; the Hamiltonian enters through which components are worth measuring.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: This paper's title is exactly the trap the brief warns about. 'Hamiltonian-aware metric' in the literature means Hamiltonian-aware METRIC ESTIMATION, not a Hamiltonian-dependent metric. If the geometry agent cites it, the distinction must be spelled out.

strand_3_information_geometry.name: Optimization Landscape Geometry in VQE for Frustrated Quantum Spin Models
strand_3_information_geometry.exact_claim: Benchmarks eight classical optimisers for exact-statevector VQE on frustrated spin models under MATCHED FUNCTION-EVALUATION BUDGETS, characterising Hamiltonian-ansatz landscapes via local minima, gradients, curvature and ground-state reachability; uses restart-based basin coverage within the same budget as a control.
strand_3_information_geometry.regime_of_validity: Spin Hamiltonians; the independent variable is the OPTIMISER, not the energy model.
strand_3_information_geometry.applies_here: YES as the methodological template and the closest published neighbour.
strand_3_information_geometry.implication: This is the paper whose METHOD the sprint should copy and whose QUESTION the sprint should differ from. Matched-evaluation-budget optimiser benchmarking with landscape characterisation is established practice - so the sprint gets no novelty credit for it, but it does get a citable protocol and a defence of brief rule 9. Adopt their restart-based basin-coverage control.
strand_3_information_geometry.verified: secondary - abstract only, OPEN THE PAPER before citing

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Finding low-energy conformations of lattice protein models by quantum annealing
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: Scientific Reports 2:571 (Perdomo-Ortiz, Dickson, Drew-Brook, Rose, Aspuru-Guzik)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Mapped HP lattice protein models onto a D-Wave quantum annealer; folding problems solved using up to 81 qubits.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART - founding paper of quantum protein folding.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: Quantum + protein folding is 14 years old. It is not novel and must not be presented as such.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Resource-efficient quantum algorithm for protein folding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: npj Quantum Information 7:38 (Robert, Barkoutsos, Woerner, Tavernelli)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Turn-based tetrahedral-lattice encoding with O(N^4) scaling; 10-amino-acid Angiotensin on 22 qubits and a 7-amino-acid neuropeptide on 9 qubits, using CVaR-based variational optimisation.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.evaluation_setting: Coarse-grained tetrahedral lattice, MJ-style pairwise interaction energies; IBM hardware.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART, and the direct ancestor of every CVaR protein-folding paper since.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: CVaR + protein folding + variational optimisation is established since 2021. The sprint's CVaR usage is standard practice, not a contribution.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Digitized-counterdiabatic quantum algorithm for protein folding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: Phys. Rev. Applied (Chandarana, Hegade, Montalban, Solano, Chen)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: dCD-VQE folded proteins of up to nine amino acids using 17 qubits with high success probability at low circuit depth.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: Counterdiabatic terms are the field's standard depth-reduction answer. If the sprint's ansatz is deep, a reviewer will ask why dCD was not tried.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: A Variable Neighbourhood Descent Heuristic for Conformational Search Using a Quantum Annealer
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: arXiv:1811.06999 / Scientific Reports (Marchand, Noori, Roberts, Rosenberg, Woods, Yildiz, Coons, Devore, Margl)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: "Using the structure of a molecule, neighbourhoods are chosen to allow for the efficient use of a binary quadratic optimizer for conformational search. The method is flexible with respect to the choice of molecular force field and the number of discretization levels in the search space, and can be further generalized to take advantage of higher-order binary polynomial optimizers."
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.evaluation_setting: Molecular conformational search on quantum-annealer-compatible binary optimisers.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Annealing / QUBO, not variational; neighbourhood-restricted so only a subset of torsions is jointly optimised at each iteration.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART for torsion-space quantum optimisation with an arbitrary classical force field.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: Discretised torsions + a real molecular force field + a quantum optimiser is EIGHT YEARS OLD. The sprint's contribution cannot be 'torsions with a real force field'. Note also their honest limitation - only a torsion SUBSET can be co-optimised - which is the same |i-j|-locality problem brief section 4 identifies.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Quantum Molecular Unfolding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: Quantum Sci. Technol. 7:035020 (Mato, Mengoni, Ottaviani, Palermo)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Formulated conformational (un)folding as a HIGH-ORDER Unconstrained Binary Optimization (HUBO) over the rotatable bonds with discrete rotation angles, then quadratised to QUBO for D-Wave 2000Q / Advantage.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Annealing; objective is maximising internal atomic distances, not a full force field.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART, and a direct technical confirmation of brief section 4.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: Independent confirmation that torsion-space objectives are natively HIGH-ORDER, not 2-local, and that the standard remedy is HUBO->QUBO quadratisation with ancillas. If the sprint takes brief route (b) - build a few-body Hamiltonian - this is the literature it must engage with, including the ancilla cost.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: QFold: Quantum Walks and Deep Learning to Solve Protein Folding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: arXiv:2101.10279 / Quantum Sci. Technol. (Casares, Campos, Martin-Delgado)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Encodes each (phi,psi) independently with a user-defined bit precision (tested 2-5 rotation bits per angle; notes ~10 deg precision needs 5-6 bits, matching AlphaFold granularity). Uses a Szegedy quantum walk as a quantum Metropolis algorithm with annealing schedules. Energies classically precomputed and supplied as an oracle. Torsion prior from Minifold, a distilled AlphaFold variant emitting von Mises distributions. Dipeptides to tetrapeptides. Reports Total-Time-to-Solution scaling with fit exponents 0.53-0.93; NO RMSD reported.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Quantum walk / Metropolis, not variational. Energies are oracle-supplied, so the physics never enters the quantum circuit.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART for torsion-bit encoding + a learned torsion prior + quantum optimisation.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: 'Discretise phi/psi into bits, take a prior from a deep model, optimise with a quantum algorithm' was published in 2021. Cite it. The sprint's differentiators must be: variational rather than Metropolis, real force field evaluated inside the loop rather than an oracle table, 9-16 residues rather than 2-4, and a proper structural benchmark rather than TTS.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: A Hybrid Quantum-AI Framework for Protein Structure Prediction on NISQ Devices
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Uses BACKBONE TORSION ENCODING that discretises K_phi and K_psi bins per residue and encodes the indices in BINARY, giving qubit count LINEAR in residue count. VQE on a 127-qubit IBM processor produces a low-resolution global energy landscape; fuses E_fuse = alpha*E_q + beta*D_ss + gamma*D_angle with NetSurfP secondary-structure and dihedral priors. Hamiltonian H = H_geom + H_steric + H_int + H_misc with MJ potentials. 75 protein fragments of 10-14 residues. Mean RMSD 4.89 A hybrid vs 6.85 A quantum-only vs 11.43 A AlphaFold3. States that quantum algorithms "often fail to accurately reproduce secondary-structure motifs or backbone dihedral angle distributions".
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: MJ interaction terms, not an all-atom force field; fragments cut from proteins rather than isolated NMR peptides; RMSD ~5 A is far from competitive.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART, and the closest published match to this project's REPRESENTATION.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: MOST IMPORTANT NOVELTY FINDING. The exact encoding - per-residue torsion bins, binary index, linear qubit scaling - was published in October 2025, on peptides of the same length, with a learned torsion/SS prior fused into the objective. 'Torsion-constrained VQE for peptides' is NOT new. Cite it prominently. The sprint's remaining differentiators are the genuine all-atom force field inside the loop, the leakage-safe sequence-conditioned torsion library, the matched-budget two-energy-model comparison, and a real benchmark - not the encoding.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Capturing Protein Free Energy Landscape using Efficient Quantum Encoding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Turn-based FCC-lattice encoding, one bead per Calpha, 18 degrees of freedom, 5(N-1) qubits for N beads. MJ potential for all non-bonded interactions plus continuity/overlap/crossing penalties. VQE with CVaR on IBM's 133-qubit Heron. 13 peptides of 6-10 residues plus chains to 20 residues. Predicted structures reach RMSD 1.22-3.11 A vs experimental references; classical MD gave 0.79-5.32 A.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Lattice, Calpha-only, MJ; small unmatched target set; only the MJ potential is evaluated - no force-field comparison.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: A LATTICE MJ CVaR-VQE already reports 1.22-3.11 A on peptides of comparable length. The sprint's <2.0 A target will be read against this. Two consequences: (a) do not claim accuracy novelty without a matched comparison; (b) their target set is small and hand-picked, so the sprint's 126-target instrument is a real methodological advantage - lead with the instrument, not the mean.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: QuPepFold
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Tetrahedral-lattice turn encoding, MJ statistical potential, hardware-efficient Rx/Ry/Rz + CNOT ansatz (3 layers for 7-mers), 2(N-3) backbone qubits + 3-5 interaction qubits (~15-18 for a 7-mer). CVaR alpha = 0.025 noiseless, 0.05 on hardware. 1,224 sequences of 6-10 residues, ~1.76M conformers. >90% fidelity in ground-state energy on IonQ Aria-1; CVaR-VQE reaches ground states ~30% faster than expectation-value VQE. NO RMSD reported. Stated limitation: "Lattice discretization oversimplifies real protein backbone geometry."
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Lattice, MJ, energy convergence as the metric - not structural accuracy.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: CVaR-VQE peptide folding now has a maintained software package. The gap they name themselves - lattice discretisation oversimplifies real backbone geometry - is precisely the gap the sprint's torsion representation fills, so quote it as motivation. Also note their honest metric choice: they report energy, not RMSD, because the lattice cannot support RMSD claims.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Quantum synergy in peptide folding: CVaR-VQE vs MD / A comparative insight into peptide folding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: Int J Biol Macromol / Quantum Inf Process 23 (Uttarkar & Niranjan)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: CVaR-VQE run over 100 iterations of 500,000 shots, contrasted with 50 ns-scale MD, plus structural alphabet analysis; CVaR-VQE reported as more effective for sampling and global optimisation than MD. A companion study covers 50 peptides of 7 amino acids.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.evaluation_setting: Short peptides, lattice encoding via the Qiskit protein-folding module.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Lattice + MJ; the comparison is quantum sampler vs classical sampler, on ONE energy model.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART - and the closest thing to a 'comparison study' in this space.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: Important distinction to make explicit in the writeup: the existing comparison literature varies the OPTIMISER with the energy model fixed. This sprint proposes to vary the ENERGY MODEL with the optimiser fixed. That is the whole novelty, and it will be lost unless stated in exactly those terms.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Peptide conformational sampling using QAOA (novelty view)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: See strand 2 row. QAOA on a simplified folding potential is matched by random sampling up to a small overhead at 20 qubits.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: The strongest published prior is NEGATIVE. Framing the sprint as a careful, controlled trainability study rather than a folding-accuracy claim is not just honest, it is the framing the literature rewards.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: The prospects of Monte Carlo antibody loop modelling on a fault-tolerant quantum computer
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: Frontiers in Drug Discovery 2:908870 / arXiv:2105.09690 (Adaszewski, Montanaro et al.)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Proposes "a specific encoding of molecular dihedral angles into registers of qubits and a method for implementing, in quantum superposition, a Markov chain Monte Carlo update step based on a classical all-atom force field". Concludes the time and space requirements are considerable.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.evaluation_setting: Resource estimate for fault-tolerant hardware; antibody CDR loops.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: FAULT-TOLERANT regime, QMCMC not variational. It is a resource estimate, not a demonstration.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART for 'dihedral angles in qubit registers + all-atom force field'.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: The specific combination 'torsion registers + all-atom force field on a quantum computer' is claimed in the literature. The sprint's genuine difference is that it EVALUATES the all-atom energy in the classical loop on sampled bitstrings (6 ms per single_point) rather than coherently, which is what makes it runnable today - and that is worth stating as a deliberate design choice, not left implicit.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: A perspective on protein structure prediction using quantum computers
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.venue: J. Chem. Theory Comput. 20 (Doga, Raubenolt, Cumbo, Joshi, DiFilippo, Qin, Blankenberg, Shehab) / arXiv:2312.00875
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Surveys quantum PSP: lattice/turn encodings dominate; MJ potentials described as "the gold standard for determining interaction energies" in quantum PSP; all-atom force fields (FF99SB) appear only in classical post-processing refinement, never inside the quantum computation. Resource estimates: 118 qubits for 22 amino acids, quadratic in sequence length; 41 aa on 433 qubits, 67 aa on 1121 qubits; ~10,000 qubits for a 141-residue protein. Explicitly notes NO empirical comparison exists showing whether coarse-grained results correlate with all-atom predictions.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Survey of the field as of late 2023.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: YES - the best single citation for the novelty gap.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: DIRECT SUPPORT FOR THE NOVELTY HYPOTHESIS. The field's own perspective names the absence of a coarse-grained-vs-all-atom comparison as an open gap, and confirms that all-atom force fields have only ever been used for classical post-processing in quantum PSP - never as the objective inside the variational loop. That is the sentence to build the contribution statement around.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Resource analysis of quantum algorithms for coarse-grained protein folding models
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Resource analysis of quantum algorithms for coarse-grained lattice folding models, including qubit and gate counts.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: If the sprint reports qubit counts for its torsion encoding (n_res*log2 k), compare directly against this paper's lattice numbers. n_res*log2(k) is LINEAR in length where the lattice turn encodings are quadratic in the Hamiltonian term count - that is a genuine, defensible, quantifiable advantage of the torsion representation and it should be stated numerically.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Quantum Algorithm for PSP Using the Face-Centered Cubic Lattice
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: First FCC-lattice implementation for quantum PSP; more expressive than the tetrahedral lattice but with a higher qubit cost.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PRIOR-ART - shows the field's response to lattice coarseness is a FINER LATTICE, not a switch to torsion space.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: Useful framing: the field is spending qubits on lattice resolution. The torsion representation spends them on real backbone geometry instead. Frame the sprint's representation choice against this trend explicitly - it is a legitimate positioning argument even though the encoding itself is not new.

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Peptide Structure Prediction Using Counter-Diabatic QAOA (CD-QAOA)
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Applies counterdiabatic QAOA to peptide structure prediction.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.regime_of_validity: Lattice (as far as could be established from the listing).
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: Confirms the area is active in 2026. Check it before submission; NOT read in this session.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.verified: secondary - NOT READ, flag before citing

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Penalty-free quantum optimization applied to lattice protein folding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Penalty-free (constraint-preserving) quantum optimisation for lattice protein folding.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.applies_here: PARTIAL - the constraint-handling idea transfers. The torsion representation is natively penalty-free (every bitstring is a valid conformation), which lattice encodings are not.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.implication: A genuine, easily-stated advantage of the torsion representation worth one sentence: no self-avoidance or chirality penalty terms are needed, so the objective carries no constraint-weight hyperparameters and no infeasible-bitstring mass. Lattice methods spend both qubits and Hamiltonian terms on this.
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.verified: secondary - NOT READ, flag before citing

strand_4_novelty_prior_art.name: Protein folding with an all-to-all trapped-ion quantum computer / 64-qubit counterdiabatic folding
strand_4_novelty_prior_art.exact_claim: Lattice protein folding executed on trapped-ion hardware with all-to-all connectivity; a 64-qubit counterdiabatic demonstration.
